mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days without regime-specific conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 2.75%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate decline below 5.0% signals labor market tightening that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in >60% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and retail sales indicates robust consumer demand, generating positive 20-day S&P 500 returns through improved earnings visibility.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in >60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS rise, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 3.0% signals active monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in non-farm payrolls supports consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, generating positive 20-day S&P 500 returns without triggering conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in >60% of periods when PAYEMS rises, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production decline below 115.0 indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings visibility, driving negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in >60% of instances when INDPRO < 115.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent positive growth in housing starts and quarterly GDP signals strong aggregate demand and economic momentum, generating positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in >60% of instances when both HOUST and GDPC1 rise, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle expansion characterized by high housing starts and low unemployment signals robust consumer spending, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns through elevated earnings expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in >60% of periods classified as late-cycle expansion (HOUST > 2200 and UNRATE < 5.0%), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
